# Standard Metric Computation

Also called: NeRF Evaluation Metrics, Photorealistic Quality Assessment, Novel View Synthesis Metrics

## Overview
Standard Metric Computation quantifies the fidelity of rendered images against ground truth references to evaluate the quality of novel-view synthesis in [Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) ([NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)) [S1, unofficial][S2][S4]. It addresses the problem of assessing rendering quality by balancing pixel-level precision, structural integrity, and perceptual similarity, providing a standardized benchmark for comparing different NeRF architectures and training procedures [S1, unofficial][S3]. What sets this family apart from raw error metrics is the inclusion of perceptual models (LPIPS) and structural models (SSIM) that correlate better with human judgment than simple pixel differences, while remaining computationally efficient enough for per-view evaluation during training loops [S2].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves computing statistical or perceptual distances between a rendered image $R$ and a ground truth image $G$. All methods in this family operate on paired images, typically normalized to $[0, 1]$ in Channel-Height-Width (CHW) or Height-Width-Channel (HWC) format [S1, unofficial][S2].

The fundamental metric is the [Mean Squared Error](#1651-mse-loss-and-psnr-conversion.md) (MSE), defined as:
$$ \text{MSE} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} (R_i - G_i)^2 $$
where $N$ is the number of pixels and $R_i, G_i$ are the pixel values [S2].

From MSE, the [Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio](#2742-psnr-metric-calculation.md) (PSNR) is derived:
$$ \text{PSNR} = -10 \cdot \frac{\log(\text{MSE})}{\log(10)} $$
or equivalently:
$$ \text{PSNR} = 10 \cdot \log_{10}\left(\frac{1}{\text{MSE}}\right) $$
[ S2, unofficial][S1, unofficial].

A critical shared principle is the handling of edge cases. If $\text{MSE} = 0$ (perfect match), PSNR becomes infinite. Implementations must handle this by capping the value, using a small epsilon, or flagging it, as infinite values disrupt aggregation [S1, unofficial]. Additionally, ground truth images often contain alpha channels (transparency), while NeRFs typically render RGB. A shared preprocessing step is [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) the ground truth [RGBA](#5142-color-packing-rgba.md) image with a white background to ensure fair comparison with the rendered RGB image [S1, unofficial][S2].

## Subtopics

### [Unified Metric Aggregation](3644-unified-metric-aggregation.md)
Computes PSNR, [Structural Similarity Index](#3650-ssim-metric-calculation.md) (SSIM), and Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS) to quantify fidelity. It differs from raw error metrics by including perceptual (LPIPS) and structural (SSIM) models that correlate better with human judgment. It aggregates per-view scores into global averages and per-view dictionaries for reporting.

### [PSNR Evaluation Pipeline](4315-psnr-evaluation-pipeline.md)
Computes PSNR on held-out test or validation splits to quantitatively assess rendering quality. It differs from training loops by disabling gradient computation, replacing active raymarching with inference-optimized variants, and aggregating pixel-wise MSE into a global mean score.

### [Masked Evaluation](7531-masked-evaluation.md)
Restricts [metric computation](#9928-metric-computation-psnr-ssim-lpips.md) to pixels visible in at least two training views, preventing evaluation on unseen regions that NeRFs cannot predict by design. It differs from sibling methods like [Unified Metric Aggregation](3644-unified-metric-aggregation.md) by explicitly excluding occluded or single-view geometry from the error calculation, thereby avoiding the artificial inflation of error metrics caused by radiance fields memorizing rather than predicting unseen content.

### [Text-Image Direction Score](13695-text-image-direction-score.md)
Estimates the semantic alignment between the direction of a text prompt modification and the resulting direction of change in the rendered image. Unlike standard pixel-wise metrics, [TIDS](#13695-text-image-direction-score.md) evaluates the *consistency of the edit* by comparing the vector difference in image space against the vector difference in text embedding space. It is primarily used to validate that a NeRF editing method successfully applies the semantic instruction specified by the user.

### Official Metrics Evaluation
**Step**
- Load render and ground truth images as tensors, handling batched or unbatched formats based on the style [S1, unofficial].
- Select metric functions based on style: `standard_3dgs` uses `loss_utils.ssim` and `batched=True`; `beta_splatting` uses `fused_ssim` and `batched=False` [S1, unofficial].
- Compute LPIPS using `lpips_module.lpips(render, gt, net_type="vgg").mean()` [S1, unofficial].
- Check that all metric values are finite [S1, unofficial].
- Compute mean metrics across all views and save to `results.json` and `per_view.json` [S1, unofficial].

### LiDAR Semantic Filtering for Evaluation
**Step**
- Identify LiDAR points that fall within the camera's field of view [S2].
- Select rays terminating on desired semantic classes (e.g., roads, sidewalks) using segmentation predictions from SegFormer [S2].
- Feed the filtered LiDAR rays into the NeRF model to perform [depth rendering](#4504-depth-rendering.md) and predict the corresponding point cloud [S2].
- Accumulate both the filtered LiDAR ground truth and the NeRF-predicted point clouds for each test frame to evaluate geometry reconstruction quality [S2].

### Nerfbusters Evaluation Protocol
**Definition**
An [evaluation procedure](#9544-monte-carlo-averaging-for-noise-reduction.md) for measuring NeRF quality at novel viewpoints by using two separate camera trajectories: one for training and one for evaluation [S3].

**Step**
- Record a video to capture the scene for the training split (10-20 seconds) [S3].
- Record a second video from a different set of viewpoints for the evaluation split [S3].
- Extract images from both videos and compute camera poses for all images [S3].
- Train a 'pseudo ground truth' model on a combination of both training and evaluation splits, and save depth, normal, and visibility maps for evaluation viewpoints [S3].
- Optimize a NeRF on the training split and evaluate at novel viewpoints using the captured evaluation images and the pseudo ground truth maps [S3].

**Parameter**
- Training videos should be around 10-20 seconds to represent typical user capture behavior [S3].

**Layout**
- The evaluation data includes: evaluation images, visibility maps, depth maps, and normal maps [S3].

**Pitfall**
- Standard benchmarks evaluate only on held-out frames from the training sequence (e.g., every 8th frame), which does not reflect quality at extreme novel viewpoints [S3].

### Negative Log Likelihood (NLL)
**Definition**
Assesses the alignment between a model's output uncertainty and actual observations, commonly used in NeRF to evaluate color value unpredictability [S4].

**Formula**
$$ NLL = -\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \log(P(c_i | x_i)) $$
[ S4].

**Parameter**
- $N$: sample count; $c_i$: measured color value; $P(c_i | x_i)$: likelihood distribution of color $c_i$ at point $x_i$ [S4].
- $P(c_i | x_i)$ is derived from forecasted color values and related uncertainty (e.g., combining model weight and scale parameters) [S4].

**Comparison**
- Lower NLL values indicate more accurate alignment of model forecasts with actual observed data [S4].

### Bootstrapped PSNR/SSIM Evaluation
**Step**
- Create a [NeRF analogy](#18133-nerf-analogies.md) and render all train and test images [S5].
- Use the rendered train images as input to train a new NeRF (using InstantNGP) [S5].
- Compute PSNR and SSIM between the previously rendered test images and the newly rendered test images from the retrained NeRF [S5].

## Background
Standard metric computation in [NeRF evaluation](#3079-nerf-evaluation-and-metric-calculation.md) originated with the seminal NeRF paper [Mildenhall et al., 2020], which established PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS as the primary benchmarks for novel-view synthesis quality [S1, unofficial]. Early benchmarks focused on held-out frames from the training sequence (e.g., every 8th frame of a video), which critics argued did not reflect quality at extreme novel viewpoints [S3]. This limitation led to the development of protocols like [Nerfbusters](#13427-nerfbusters.md), which introduced separate training and evaluation video captures to assess performance on truly novel views [S3].

The inclusion of LPIPS, a learned perceptual metric, addressed the discrepancy between pixel-wise error and human perception, as PSNR often correlates poorly with subjective quality [S1, unofficial][S4]. More recently, metrics have expanded beyond photorealism to include semantic alignment (TIDS) and geometric consistency (Masked Evaluation, LiDAR filtering) to support text-guided editing and large-scale urban reconstruction [S1, unofficial][S2].
